preserved_objections.basis: Microcapsules containing isocyanate and polyol healing agents would likely react prematurely during vulcanization or under normal operating temperatures, preventing proper healing functionality as the reactive components would be consumed before damage occurs.

The proposed solution does not address the primary boundary condition of constant cyclic loading from traffic, which would continuously damage the healing mechanism faster than it can repair, especially at 5-10% microcapsule concentration.

The candidate's evidence bundle includes a paper on "Fatigue life analysis of laminated elastomeric bearing pad" which indicates that failure occurs through progressive delamination and crack propagation mechanisms that cannot be addressed by localized microcrack healing.

The proposed microencapsulation technology at 5-10% loading would significantly alter the mechanical properties of the elastomer matrix, likely reducing load-bearing capacity and violating the fundamental performance requirements of bridge bearing pads.

The testable prediction fails to define critical parameters such as healing efficiency metrics, crack size thresholds for effective repair, and long-term stability of healing agents under environmental exposure.
